uses.quote: There are few restrictions on the use of generative AI to help your personal studies.
uses.anchor: Using generative AI at UWE Bristol

uses.quote: If you are guided to use generative AI in your assessments or assignments, you will need to acknowledge its use through referencing.
uses.anchor: Referencing the use of generative AI

uses.quote: Do not submit AI generated work in assessments without appropriate acknowledgement.
please suggest some prompts that I might want to use to help me brainstorm ideas around running a successful project.
You can use generative AI to search for information by providing a query or a prompt that describes what you are looking for.
create a visual representation of a concept.
You can test your knowledge by creating questions, quizzes, or exercises based on your own study notes.
To function as a learning aid, you will need to provide the generative AI with a specific query or a prompt that describes what you want to learn or improve.
To help you with organising your work, you may want to ask generative AI to create a to-do list, a timeline, or a checklist for your work.
You can use generative AI to make a study plan by providing a query or a prompt that describes what kind of approach you want to take.
Remember that generative AI is often inaccurate, creating false references, out-of-date detail and false information (known as ‘hallucinations’). Always check your results.

It is important to remember that it is an academic offence to download material from the web and submit it as your own work, or submit work created by using AI tools without appropriate acknowledgement.
